gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at 2026-11-17 maker prices, ChatGPT's highest-efficiency large pick (EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3, 93%) costs about $0.74 per delivered Wh and is sold out on EcoFlow US until late January, while the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (96%, in stock at $899) delivers at about $0.45 per Wh and the DELTA 3 Classic (93%) at about $0.48 per Wh after a drop to $459.
standout_why: wattpowerstation.com/real-capacity (cited in all three chats) already lists brand-store prices checked 2026-11-09 and a '$ per usable Wh' column for 39 models (Elite 200 V2 $0.45, DELTA 3 Classic $0.51 at $479, Dabbsson 2000L $0.34, DELTA Pro 3 marked 'Sold out' with no figure). So the price-per-delivered-Wh idea is not new. What it lacks: today's prices (DELTA 3 Classic now $459, AC180 now $549 vs $499), the DELTA Pro 3 restock date (late January, per EcoFlow), and any per-Wh figure for DELTA Pro 3 or Jackery Explorer 1000 v2. OutdoorGearLab (cited) prices DELTA Pro 3 at $3,699 and computes $0.90/Wh on rated, not measured, capacity; backuppowerfinder.com shows no prices at all.
decides: Confirms BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 as the pick: highest measured share (96%, one CNET test at 480 W) and among the lowest cost per delivered Wh of ChatGPT's picks ($899 / 1,989 Wh = $0.45), in stock today. It demotes ChatGPT's second pick, the DELTA Pro 3: it cannot be bought from EcoFlow US now and costs ~65% more per delivered Wh. For ~1 kWh buyers, the DELTA 3 Classic (93%, $459) beats the carded Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (86-87%, $549.99 at B&H, special order) on both share and price per delivered Wh. Outside ChatGPT's picks, Dabbsson 2000L is cheapest per delivered Wh ($0.34) but its 92% rests on two tests.
